newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia presidential elections on Sept 21-official.
newsitem.headline: Serbia presidential elections on Sept 21-official.

text.p: Presidential elections in Serbia will be held on September 21, the vice-president of the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) said on Wednesday.
The vote would choose a successor to strongman Slobodan Milosevic, who became president of federal Yugoslavia -- comprising Serbia and tiny Montenegro -- earlier in the day.

"Elections will be scheduled within the required legal deadline of 60 days," Milorad Vucelic, vice-president of Milosevic's SPS, told Reuters. He said the vote would be held on September 21 and the SPS would name its candidate on Friday.
"You will know the candidate after the (SPS) main board's session on Friday. I think Zoran Lilic will make an excellent candidate," Vucelic said.

Lilic was the president of Yugoslavia until Milosevic took over the office. Diplomats said Lilic performed well in the mostly ceremonial post of federal president and has remained untarnished by any scandal.
He was considered a Milosevic mounthpiece but at times offered voiced personal opinion which differed from his mentor -- just enough to make him palatable to the broader voting public, one said.
Vucelic did not expect any changes in the federal and the Serbian government before elections in Serbia.
"We are not planing any personnel changes. Why should we? Things are going well."
